_note: One unit = one lesson path in five steps. Write 'God' (the Muslim view shows 'Allah'). Verses by ref only (shown from src/data/ayahs.json); hadith by id only (shown from src/data/hadith.json). 'about' lines are our own words, never a translation.

intro.muslim: Musa travelled to meet a servant of God who had been given knowledge from Him. The man did three strange things, and Musa could not keep quiet. Then the hidden reasons were explained. Watch.
intro.curious: Musa, known in the Bible as Moses, travelled to meet a servant of God, known in Muslim tradition as al-Khidr, who had been given special knowledge. The man did three strange things, and Musa could not stay quiet. Then the hidden reasons were explained.

muslim.situation: You didn't get into the course you worked hard for. A friend with lower grades did. You're crushed.

options.label: Decide there's no point trying at anything anymore.
options.feedback: That's a heavy feeling. Musa's journey shows there can be good hidden in what hurts.

options.label: Grieve it, say "God decreed, and He does what He wills," and look for the next good step.
options.feedback: That's exactly what the Prophet ﷺ taught: strive, accept what God decrees, and keep going without "if only".

options.label: Keep replaying it: if only I'd done this, if only I'd done that.
options.feedback: Very human, but the Prophet ﷺ warned that "if only" opens a door to despair. See the teaching.

options.label: Pretend you never wanted it anyway.
options.feedback: It protects you a little, but it isn't true. Accepting the decree means admitting it hurts and trusting God anyway.

heading.muslim: What God teaches about His decree

quran.about: Musa finds a servant of God who had been given mercy and knowledge from God.
The servant explains the hidden reasons for the boat, the boy and the wall, and says he did none of it by his own will.
God created everything in due measure.
Nothing happens except that it was written before; so do not despair over what you miss, nor gloat over what you are given.
You may dislike something that is good for you, and love something that is bad for you. God knows, and you do not.

hadith.about: Strive for what benefits you, then accept what God decrees without "if only".
No one can help or harm you except by what God has already written.

insights.text: Belief in the decree is often explained in four parts: God knows everything, He wrote it all down, nothing happens except by His will, and He created all things, including what people do. People still choose, and are responsible for their choices.
Belief in the decree is not giving up. The Prophet ﷺ said: strive for what benefits you, seek God's help, and don't give up (Muslim 2664). Effort comes first; acceptance comes after.

check.q: Why did the servant of God damage the boat?
options: A king was seizing every sound boat, so a damaged one would be left to its poor owners
check.why: The boat belonged to poor fishermen; a king was seizing every sound boat (18:79).

check.q: Why did he rebuild the wall in the unfriendly town?
options: A treasure for two orphans lay under it, kept safe until they grew up
check.why: Under the wall lay treasure for two orphans whose father had been righteous (18:82).

options: We always know what is best for us
We may dislike something that is good for us
check.why: You may dislike something that is good for you; God knows and you do not.

check.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ say to say when something goes wrong?
options: If only I had done things differently
God has decreed, and what He wills He does
check.why: Say, "God has decreed, and what He wills He does," for "if only" opens the door to Satan's work.

check.q: Does belief in the decree mean you shouldn't try?
options: Yes, everything is fixed, so effort is pointless
No: strive for what benefits you, then accept the outcome
check.why: The same hadith says: strive for what benefits you and do not give up.

reflection.muslim: Think of something that hurt at the time but led somewhere good. What might God be preparing through what's hard now?
reflection.curious: Has something you didn't want ever turned out for the best? How does that change how you see what's going wrong now?
